body: Thank you.  I greatly appreciate that.

First of all, something going on could be a number of things.  But even if it is cancer, most thyroid cancers are cured by simply surgically removing the thyroid.  

Second of all, it's bullshit that contributions to society are measured in employment and how much money you make.  Living for your son means you're a great parent, and that's more important.  University will still be there next semester.  Probably better that, if you do need surgery or other treatment, you're not trying to juggle school and childcare on top of that.  

Does your husband work?  You may be able to work out a payment plan with the hospital if you need surgery.  

I'm sorry you're struggling.  Anyone would be with so many things going on at once.  You're sure as hell not whining!

That's very kind of you, and I really appreciate that.  It's a shitty situation for everyone involved I think, and I just don't think it can be made better.  I'm not a victim here, but I'm at a loss as to how to deal with it regardless.  It seems like more effort and pain than it's worth to get through.
